item.title: Aso Caldera & Daikanbō Viewpoint — Guide
item.description: The Aso caldera, in the heart of Aso-Kujū National Park, is one of the largest volcanic calderas in the world — a vast basin some 25 km across, ringed by mountains, holding a green landscape of towns, rice fields and grasslands within its walls. Touring it by car is one of the great scenic drives of Kyushu. The classic viewpoint is Daikanbō, a lookout on the caldera’s northern rim offering a jaw-dropping panorama over the entire basin, the central volcanic peaks and the outer rim — from here the row of central cones is said to resemble a ‘sleeping Buddha’ reclining on the plain.

item.title: Goshikidai Plateau: Scenic Heights over the Sea — Guide
item.description: Goshikidai is a broad lava plateau rising between Takamatsu and Sakaide on the Kagawa coast, its name (‘five-colour heights’) referring to five hills. A scenic road crosses the plateau, linking viewpoints, walking trails, a planetarium and quiet woodland, with sweeping panoramas over the Seto Inland Sea and its islands. From its western edge there are especially fine views of the great Seto Ohashi bridge striding across the water toward Honshu, magnificent at sunset and when lit at night.

item.title: Himuka / Hyuga Coast Scenic Drive — Guide
item.description: Miyazaki’s coastline offers superb scenic driving not only south along the Nichinan Coast but also north around the Hyuga area, where the dramatic ‘Himuka’ coast features some of the prefecture’s most striking sea scenery. The star attraction is Cape Umagase (Umagase), where sheer cliffs of columnar volcanic rock — formed by ancient lava flows and eroded into remarkable regular pillars — drop dramatically into the deep blue sea, viewed from clifftop walkways and lookouts.

item.title: Kouri Island & Bridge — Guide
item.description: Kouri Island (Kourijima), a small round island off the Motobu Peninsula in northern Okinawa, is one of the island’s most beloved scenic spots, famous above all for the spectacular drive across the Kouri Bridge that connects it to the mainland. Nearly 2 km long and flanked by dazzling turquoise and emerald sea, the bridge is a highlight in itself, and the view from either end is unforgettable. On the island, Kouri Beach beside the bridge offers clear, shallow water perfect for swimming and photos, while on the north coast the famous ‘Heart Rock’ — two rock formations that together frame a heart shape — is a hugely popular photo spot, especially with couples.

item.title: Shikoku Karst: A Highland of Cattle and Sky — Guide
item.description: The Shikoku Karst is one of Japan’s three great karst plateaus, a striking highland running along the Ehime–Kochi border at around 1,400 metres. Here rolling green grassland stretches to the horizon, studded with weathered white limestone rocks and grazed by cattle in summer, under enormous open skies — a landscape utterly unlike the rest of mountainous Shikoku. A scenic skyline road runs along the plateau, passing viewpoints, a campground and windmills, with sweeping panoramas over range after range of Shikoku’s mountains.

item.title: The Nichinan Coast — Guide
item.description: The Nichinan Coast (Nichinan Kaigan) is a beautiful stretch of subtropical coastline running south from Miyazaki city, and one of the most scenic drives in Kyushu. Following the shore along Route 220, the road winds past a succession of dramatic capes, blue Pacific bays, rocky islets, phoenix palm-lined avenues and lush green hills, with viewpoints and rest stops along the way. It links some of Miyazaki’s most famous sights, including the cave shrine of Udo Jingū set in the seaside cliffs, and further south, Cape Toi with its herds of wild horses grazing on the headland.

item.title: Echigo Mountains & Sea of Japan Coastline: A Landscape of Contrasts — Guide
item.description: Niigata’s geography is defined by a striking contrast between the snow-capped Echigo mountain ranges inland, among Japan’s snowiest regions, and the rugged Sea of Japan coastline stretching along the prefecture’s western edge. Scenic coastal roads wind past dramatic cliffs, fishing villages and sunset viewpoints over the Sea of Japan, while inland routes climb into the mountains through forests and terraced rice paddies, together showcasing the full range of Niigata’s varied natural landscape within a single road trip.

item.title: Kuzuryu River Gorge: A Scenic Ravine Along Fukui's Longest River — Guide
item.description: The Kuzuryu River, named after a mythical nine-headed dragon (kuzuryu) said to have once dwelled in the region, is Fukui’s longest river, and carves a scenic gorge through the inland mountains as it winds toward the coast. The gorge offers a dramatic scenic drive or walk along the water, with steep forested slopes rising on either side, and the autumn foliage season transforms the ravine into one of the region’s most striking seasonal landscapes.

item.title: Bandai-Azuma Skyline & Nishi-Azuma Sky Valley: Fukushima's Great Scenic Drives — Guide
item.description: The Bandai-Azuma Skyline and the neighbouring Nishi-Azuma Sky Valley are two of Tohoku’s most celebrated scenic mountain drives, winding roughly 30 km combined through the volcanic Azuma range at elevations over 1,600 m. Each curve reveals a new lookout over jagged peaks, steaming volcanic vents and, come October, some of the region’s most vivid autumn foliage — a fiery tapestry of maple and beech that draws road-trippers from across Japan. Both routes are seasonal toll roads, closed by snow each winter.

item.title: Zao Okama Crater Lake: Yamagata's Emerald Volcano — Guide
item.description: Zao’s Okama crater lake is one of Japan’s most spectacular volcanic phenomena — an almost perfectly circular caldera filled with water of an otherworldly emerald-green colour caused by dissolved sulphur compounds. The Zao Echo Line toll road reaches the rim, making this one of Japan’s most accessible volcanic craters, with the colour shifting between deep teal and bright lime with the weather. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Zao, Yamagata (Miyagi border) Hours Echo Line ~Apr–Nov, daytime Admission Toll road fee applies Time needed About 1 hour Best time Summer–autumn; clear days for best colour What to See The near-perfectly circular emerald-green crater lake.
